notes.heading: Book Introduction - 2 Chronicles
notes.body: Chronicles This book continues the history begun in First Chronicles. It falls into eighteen divisions, by reigns, from Solomon to the captivities; records the division of the kingdom of David under Jeroboam and Rehoboam, and is marked by an ever growing apostasy, broken temporarily by reformations under Asa, 14-16; Jehoshaphat, 17:1-19; Joash, 24; Hezekiah, 29-32; and Josiah, 34,35. But the religious state of the people, even at the best, is described in Isaiah 1-5. The events recorded in Second Chronicles cover a period of 427 years. (Ussher).

notes.heading: court
notes.body: The tabernacle had no "court of priests."

notes.heading: cloud
notes.body: See 2 Chronicles 5:11-13. (See Scofield "Exodus 40:34").

notes.heading: river
notes.body: "The river," i.e. Euphrates, to the border of Egypt, but not to the "river of Egypt." Cf. Genesis 15:18 yet to be fulfilled:

notes.heading: rest of
notes.body: These books have perished. 1 Kings 11:29.

notes.heading: Israel
notes.body: "Israel," the ten tribes other than Judah and Benjamin, often called "Israel" in distinction from Judah. The division of the kingdom marks an epoch of great importance in the history of the nation. Henceforth it is "a kingdom divided against itself." Matthew 12:25. The two kingdoms are to be reunited in the future kingdom. ; Isaiah 11:10-13; Jeremiah 23:5,6; Ezekiel 37:15-28. See "Kingdom" (O.T.), (See Scofield "Genesis 1:26") See Scofield "Zechariah 12:8". (N.T.), ; Luke 1:31; 1 Corinthians 15:28. "Israel," ; Genesis 12:2,3; Romans 11:26.

notes.heading: devils
notes.body: Lit. "hairy ones," i.e. satyrs, Isaiah 13:21.

notes.heading: Michaiah
notes.body: Probably a grandchild of Absalom, called Abishalom, Cf. 2 Chronicles 11:20; 1 Kings 15:2.

notes.heading: places
notes.body: Cf. (See Scofield "1 Kings 3:2") See Scofield "1 Kings 15:14".

notes.heading: when Asa
notes.body: Chapter 14 describes the outward prosperity of the kingdom, and Asa's superficial reformation; chapter 15 the true reformation.

notes.heading: mother
notes.body: i.e. grandmother. 1 Kings 15:13,

notes.heading: Israel
notes.body: i.e. the northen or ten-tribe kingdom.

notes.heading: to Asa
notes.body: i.e. none of his subjects. 2 Chronicles 16:5,6; 15:9.

notes.heading: father
notes.body: After the Jewish custom of calling a family, or tribal head, father; e.g. John 8:53.

notes.heading: Israel
notes.body: i.e. the ten-tribe kingdom.

notes.heading: Jehoram
notes.body: Jehoram reigned for a time as co-king with his father. 2 Kings 8:16.

notes.heading: began
notes.body: Began, that is, as co-king. 2 Chronicles 22:2 (See Scofield "2 Chronicles 21:1").

notes.heading: Elijah
notes.body: See Elijah history. 1 Kings 17:1; 2 Kings 2:12.

notes.heading: Jehoahaz
notes.body: Called Ahaziah, 2 Chronicles 22:1,6 and Azariah:

notes.heading: Ahaziah
notes.body: where he is called Jehoahaz. 2 Chronicles 21:17.

notes.heading: Ephraim
notes.body: Used in a collective sense for the northern ten-tribe kingdom, called also "Israel."

notes.heading: reconciliation
notes.body: Or, an offering. (See Scofield "Daniel 9:24")

notes.heading: second month
notes.body: i.e. May; 2 Chronicles 30:13,15.
